title: Files added before the one-file-per-hash change (v3) never got a hash: adding the same file again stores a second copy and Files shows it twice — 12 of the copy's 25 files
detail: Copy account: 12 of 25 records in kurenai-os-files have hash null (added July-October 2026; 11 still hold their bytes, among them 10 CS 4.5.1.1 papers/schemes and an IT handout). Re-adding one of them (its own blob as a new File) through KOS.attach.add, (1) to another topic → {linked:false}, record 31 stored with a real hash, the old one still null; (2) to the SAME topic → {linked:false}, record 32 stored. Files then lists both copies (two size groups duplicated) — invariant 150 says one file per hash with many links. The same holds for the paper twin rule (files.js:76 twin = r.hash && hashes[r.hash]): a Paper-library PDF with the same bytes never joins such a file. Test records removed afterwards (count back to 25).
rootCause: js/modules/attachments.js:73-86 — the v3 upgrade back-fills fileId, updatedAt and linkKeys for old rows but never computes hash; add() (attachments.js:169-192) looks up the hash index, which an old row (hash null) can never match. Only Paper-library records get a hash back-fill (js/core/exampapers.js:216-220).
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/copy/files-mac-copy-dupe-readd.png; eval nullHash 12/25, add → {id:31, linked:false}, add same topic → {id:32, linked:false}; js/modules/attachments.js:73
fix: A one-time idle back-fill: for records with a blob and no hash, hashOf(blob) → updateFile(rec.fileId, r.hash = h), then merge any two records that now share a hash through the existing link path (KOS.repairs if it merges); mirror exampapers.js:216.
